name: MiniMax-M1: Scaling Test-Time Compute Efficiently with Lightning Attention
problem: Long-context reasoning models chain many thousands of intermediate reasoning tokens, and paying full KV-cache attention cost for every one of those tokens does not scale, so test-time compute scaling was blocked by decode cost rather than by context length.
mechanism: Hybrid MoE plus lightning attention, with the architecture inherited from MiniMax-Text-01: 456B total parameters, 45.9B activated per token, native 1M-token context, which the paper states is 8x the context size of DeepSeek R1. The novel claim in THIS paper is not the architecture but the serving-side consequence: because lightning attention carries a constant-size state, the mechanism enables efficient scaling of test-time compute, i.e. the per-token cost of emitting long chains of reasoning does not grow with how much context has already accumulated. That is the cleanest statement in this slice of why constant-state attention changes an economics problem (reasoning-token volume) rather than only a memory problem.
